recommendation: Keep the commit as the bounded FHIR-34134 fix. Handle FHIR-54843 separately for the broader R6 changes such as 0..* cardinality and an example body-site binding.
issue_request: FHIR-34134 was Published with resolution Persuasive with Modification for R5. It requested support for patient-associated devices with anatomical location; the accepted resolution changed the Device association model to include humanSubject and bodyStructure, with bodyStructure typed as CodeableReference(BodyStructure).
initial_application: Commit b446711a78 renamed Device.associationState to Device.association and added Device.association.bodyStructure as CodeableReference(BodyStructure). Jira comment evidence points to 6a6ee72b71 as a follow-up correction. Later FHIR-38904 work moved the patient-identifying association backbone out of Device and into DeviceAssociation, leaving the old Device.association source commented out.
additional_context: FHIR-38904 was a later Published OO decision that removed Device.association and created DeviceAssociation to avoid patient-identifying information in reusable Device instances; its proposed replacement structure still listed bodyStructure as CodeableReference(BodyStructure). The current build includes DeviceAssociation in source/fhir.ini and Device boundaries text directs association use there. FHIR-54206 and FHIR-54843 separately identify broader BodyStructure-pattern work for DeviceAssociation.bodyStructure, including cardinality and binding, but those later R6 issues were not decided in this seed commit.
reconciliation: Changed source/deviceassociation/structuredefinition-DeviceAssociation.xml so DeviceAssociation.bodyStructure uses CodeableReference with targetProfile BodyStructure instead of Reference, preserving current 0..1 cardinality and existing example compatibility.
source_changes: source/deviceassociation/structuredefinition-DeviceAssociation.xml: DeviceAssociation.bodyStructure type changed from Reference to CodeableReference while retaining targetProfile BodyStructure and 0..1 cardinality.
